text:
maya: Heads up — trying to onboard a hybrid model (OrionConv-7B: Mistral-style attention with Llama-derived FF/proj). Converter ran, weights aligned, but longctx summarization fails hard after int4 quant.
liam: ugh. what does "fails hard" look like? numbers?
maya: on our multitask eval set (chat-summary longform) rouge-L drops ~12 pts vs fp16 baseline; perplexity +40 on 2k context. Short context (<256) fine.
jorge: could be positional map or KV-proj ordering. hybrid conv1d adapters sometimes change head ordering during export. Did the converter emit any warnings?
maya: only this: 
```
WARNING: pos_map: non-monotonic indices at layer 9
WARNING: conv_proj: inferred head_grouping != model_spec.heads
```
nora: that usually means the code guessed head grouping from tensor shapes. If head_grouping differs the rotary/rope mapping can be misaligned across layers (headwise scale mismatch).
liam: do we have a quick check diff between fp16 and quant embeddings/kv caches? even a single head shuffle will show up as correlated cosine drop.
maya: ran a per-head cosine between fp16 and int4 projection outputs. Layers 8-11 have ~0.85 instead of ~0.99. others are fine.
jorge: yep — head permutation. Two common fixes: 1) canonicalize head order in converter (permute weights to canonical layout) 2) adjust positional mapping to match runtime rotary dims.
nora: for (1) we need to pick canonical ordering we use in runtime (ours is [0..H-1] contiguous); some exporters interleave adapter heads. For (2) check if the converter applied per-head stride.
maya: putting a small script on the converter to enforce contiguous head layout got short-context metrics back to baseline but long-context still bad. suspecting subtle rope phase offsets (headwise scale).
liam: can you dump KV cache cosine decay across timesteps? if rope phase is off, reconstruction error should grow with position index.
maya: attached small log excerpt: 
```
kv_cosine_layer9: t0=0.995 t128=0.912 t512=0.601 t1024=0.33
kv_cosine_layer12: t0=0.998 t128=0.997 t512=0.992 t1024=0.989
```
liam: layer9 clearly decaying — rope mismatch. Not quant noise.
jorge: interesting that layer12 looks fine. Could be a hybrid layout where certain residual adapters use a different rotary base freq. Some Mistral-derived blocks use a doubled freq for mid layers.
nora: did the converter preserve rotary base (freq) metadata? many model files omit it.
maya: converter set base=10000 by default. but original config had "rotary_freqs": [10000, 5000] in model card.
liam: there it is. if layer9 expected 5000 but we used 10000, phase drift will scale with position — matches the decay with position.
jorge: two paths: update converter to read rotary_freqs per-block when available; or at runtime allow per-layer rotary scaling override via model metadata.
maya: quick experiment: re-export with per-layer freq (set layer9=5000), int4 quant, run smoke. Rouge-L up by 9 pts (still -3 vs fp16).
liam: that reduction might be quantization noise interacting with small-scale rotaries. Try per-head clamp calibration (symmetric vs asymmetric) or per-channel quant.
nora: also check tokenization/vocab alignment. hybrid converters sometimes remap sentinel or bos tokens; long-context summarization is very sensitive to EOS token mapping.
maya: token ids match on a small sample. but I did see an off-by-one in pad sentinel mapping for converter version 0.2.1 — fixed in 0.2.2.
jorge: good catch. If both rope freq and sentinel were wrong, they compound.
maya: next steps I propose: 1) update converter to read per-layer rotary metadata and enforce canonical head order 2) run int4 calibration with per-channel scaling on attention projections for layers showing decay 3) run a canary on dedicated pool with fallback to fp16 qwen-variant for traffic shaping 4) add an eval that specifically measures cosine decay vs position and alerts if <0.9 at t=256
liam: +1. also add a small automated check when adding new model to registry: compare kv_cosine curve fp16->quant and require monotonic high similarity on early t.
nora: for rollout, canary on Dedicated with 10% traffic and synthetic longctx prompts (docs->summary). If regression detected, automatic rollback to fp16 or previous model id.
maya: I'll push a converter patch and a per-layer metadata read. dropping a draft PR once CI runs.
ciabot: maya pushed branch "orion/posmap-freq-fix" with 3 commits, CI queued.
deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled to eng-dedicated cluster at 2026-03-24T15:00:00Z, will route 10% traffic to model:orionconv-7b:v2-canary. automatic rollback enabled.
liam: thanks — offer to help with calibration sweep tomorrow.
maya: appreciate it. Will post update after PR + canary results.
